requirement: Accept machine fault events from the telematics platform through a REST API.
Accept customer parts orders from the e-commerce storefront through a REST API.
Validate every inbound message against the canonical schema and reject malformed messages with a reason code.
Log severity 1 (informational) faults for monitoring without creating orders.
Map known fault codes to the parts kit defined in the ERP fault catalog.
When a fault code is missing or unknown, diagnose from the symptom note with the AI recommender and send predictions below the confidence threshold to a service advisor for manual review.
Source each order line from the machine's assigned dealer first, then from another dealer in the same region, otherwise backorder it.
Create exactly one ERP sales order per accepted message with header, lines, status and fulfillment type.
Retry transient Dealer Management System failures up to 3 times with exponential backoff.
Send messages that cannot be processed to a dead letter queue with a reason code and allow replay of replayable messages once the cause is fixed.
Never create more than one order for the same message id (idempotency for resends and double clicks).
Reject storefront orders for parts not in the ERP catalog and hold orders whose price differs from the ERP price list by more than 1 percent.
Do not create a second order for the same machine and fault while an order from the last 7 days is still open.
Record an audit trail of every processing step that can be retrieved by message id.
Provide an operations dashboard with volumes, outcomes, dead letters, fulfillment mix and AI performance.
95th percentile processing latency is under 50 ms per message across 1000 messages.
No partial orders: if any step fails all inventory reservations for that message roll back.
Inventory never goes negative and reserved quantity never exceeds on-hand quantity.
Inputs are validated by pattern and type, all database access is parameterized, and injection attempts are rejected without side effects.
AI diagnoses that create orders automatically are at least 85 percent precise on held-out data.
Every received message ends in exactly one terminal outcome; no message is lost.
Business rule thresholds are configurable in one place without code changes to processing logic.
